findings.summary: --import path is resolved and passed to import_geometry without any check that it is a regular file inside an allowed location; a crafted path (e.g. UNC \\host\share or a device path) is read by the server.
findings.scenario: Blender add-on sends --import '\\attacker\share\x.step' -> server opens remote SMB path (credential leak / hang)
findings.fix: Reject non-local paths (UNC, device names) and require Path.is_file() before import.

findings.summary: plane_and_blend_labels: 'cut' expression uses operator precedence — `plane_patch[patch[a]] & (patch[a] != patch[b]) | plane_patch[patch[b]] & (patch[a] != patch[b])` is fine, but `own = np.where(plane_patch[patch[a]], a, b)[cut]` picks a when a is plane; if both a and b are plane patches (different patches) it picks a — acceptable.
findings.scenario: Two adjacent plane patches both flagged plane: cut True, own=a, other=b; smooth test compares normals of two coplanar patches (dot ~1) so frac counts them as smooth, potentially suppressing a legitimate plane split.
findings.fix: Exclude pairs where both are plane patches from the smooth-fraction test.

findings.summary: split_blended_faces rebuilds the model with gmsh.model.remove()/add() and re-adds nodes only to the first surface, but the returned groups are used to build a surface loop; if labels.max()+1 <= len(groups) it returns the original groups while the model was already mutated? No—the early return happens before remove().
findings.scenario: labels.max()+1 > len(groups): model is rebuilt; but the caller then does addSurfaceLoop over the new surfaces — OK. However the rebuilt model loses the original surface tags used elsewhere (e.g. key_of mapping in the discrete branch).
findings.fix: Verify callers only use returned groups; otherwise keep tag mapping.

findings.summary: fatigue_life_min_away computed via support_peak(nodes, fixed, -f['life']) — support_peak returns 'max_vm_away_pa' which is the max of the negated life, i.e. -min life away; negating gives min life away. But if support_peak returns None for max_vm_away_pa (no away nodes), float(None) raises TypeError.
findings.scenario: Small mesh where all nodes are on the support: support_peak returns max_vm_away_pa=None -> float(None) crash.
findings.fix: Guard: only set fatigue_life_min_away when the away value is not None.

findings.summary: sweep_scratch deletes any directory under <scratch root>/runs not referenced by this workspace and older than 7 days, including runs of another workspace/user on the same machine (e.g. shared Public folder).
findings.scenario: Two users share C:\Users\Public\NovaSolverStudio; user A's sweep deletes user B's 8-day-old scratch run still needed for a queued job
findings.fix: Only sweep runs whose pointer file lives in this workspace, or tag runs with the owning workspace and skip others.

findings.summary: Recursive _project call passes k2 up to len(Xm); with many misses this re-runs the full O(P*k) Newton loop and can recurse again, causing very long runtimes or recursion depth issues on large meshes.
findings.scenario: 100k slave nodes, 50k master tris, all miss at k=8 -> k2=50000, full projection over all elements per point
findings.fix: Cap k2 (e.g. 256) and iterate with growing k instead of one full pass.

findings.summary: Direct spsolve is now used for all nonlinear runs up to 120k dof regardless of contact; on machines with little RAM this can raise non-MemoryError failures (e.g. SuperLU out-of-memory as RuntimeError) that are not caught.
findings.scenario: 38k-dof plastic model on 4 GB RAM -> spsolve raises RuntimeError, not MemoryError -> run crashes instead of falling back to AMG
findings.fix: Catch RuntimeError/Exception from spsolve and fall through to the iterative path.

findings.summary: split_blended_faces: after gmsh.model.remove()/add(), the returned groups are new surface tags, but the caller in import_stl uses them for addSurfaceLoop — fine. However the discrete branch earlier (line ~130) returns key_of mapping; the non-discrete branch returns None for key_of, so face keys are lost after splitting.
findings.scenario: STL import with blended faces: split_blended_faces returns groups but key_of is None, so downstream face naming by key fails.
findings.fix: Return a key mapping consistent with the split groups.

findings.summary: verification['reference'] set to None when not extrapolated, but downstream code (e.g. UI) may compute error_pct from reference; also `ref['reference'] != ref['computed']` fallback is a float equality that is almost always True, so the None branch rarely triggers.
findings.scenario: Oscillating convergence levels with f_ext None: reference stays as levels[-1] value (== computed), so error_pct=0 shown as if perfect agreement.
findings.fix: Use ref.get('extrapolated') is False explicitly, not float inequality.

findings.summary: Hertz cylinder axis_point uses hb+R but the test asserts axis_point[1] == radius + height/1e3, and the mesher's cylinder axis may not be at y=hb+R; if the mesher places the cylinder elsewhere the descriptor is wrong.
findings.scenario: hertz-cylinder with height 20 mm, radius 25 mm -> axis_point y = 0.045 m; if the mesher's cylinder axis is at y=hb (block top) the face descriptor points to the wrong axis, so bearing/cylindrical BCs and contact normals are computed about the wrong line.
findings.fix: Derive axis_point from the same geometry the mesher uses (e.g. geometry.dims / the cylinder builder) instead of re-deriving hb+R here.

findings.summary: _scratch_run validates the pointer's parent chain but not that the pointer file itself is inside the case folder; rglob over a case folder could follow a symlink/junction to an arbitrary of_location.txt and rmtree an unrelated runs/ dir.
findings.scenario: Case folder contains a junction to another workspace's job dir with of_location.txt -> remove_scratch deletes that other run
findings.fix: Resolve the pointer path and require it to be under the case folder before trusting it.

findings.summary: primary_quantity returns fatigue_sf_min_away for fatigue-bar when on support; but the study's peak_vm_pa and convergence still track max_vm which is singular — the study may pass on SF while stress singularity warning is separate. Acceptable but the 'fatigue_sf' response name is used for the study quantity while results.py card uses fatigue_sf_min_away too — consistent.
findings.scenario: fatigue-bar with fixed x0: study tracks away SF, converges; fine.

findings.summary: Verified gate chip now shows gate.reference/gate.mesh based on verified_by, but if verified_by is undefined/null it falls to gate.mesh, mislabeling reference-verified cases.
findings.scenario: Case with gates.verified=true and verified_by missing -> chip shows 'Mesh verified' instead of 'Verified'.
findings.fix: Default to a generic verified label when verified_by is not 'reference'.

findings.summary: delete() calls remove_scratch(d) before shutil.rmtree; if remove_scratch raises (e.g. missing dir), the case is never deleted.
findings.scenario: Scratch dir already gone -> remove_scratch raises FileNotFoundError -> delete fails.
findings.fix: Wrap remove_scratch in try/except or check existence.

findings.summary: Hardcoded tool count 30 will break smoke test whenever tools are added/removed; brittle assertion.
findings.scenario: Adding a 31st MCP tool -> smoke test fails despite correct behavior.
findings.fix: Assert a minimum count or check specific tool names instead.

findings.summary: Mesh study level label uses t('export.size.'+l['size']) without a fallback; if a level size key is missing in a language the raw key is printed.
findings.scenario: conv level size 'coarse' missing in zh -> report shows 'export.size.coarse'
findings.fix: Fall back to l['size'] when the key is absent.

findings.summary: _gates_line third-gate text: when verified_by is set but verified is false and verified_by=='reference', the expression yields 'does not match reference' correctly, but when verified_by is None and verified true it prints 'mesh convergence not checked' contradicting verified=yes.
findings.scenario: gates {ran:yes,converged:yes,verified:yes,verified_by:None} -> line says 'mesh convergence not checked'
findings.fix: Handle verified true with no verified_by explicitly.

findings.summary: GateStepper reads noCheck from !results.verification but the verified tooltip then says 'tipTodo' even when the gate is on via a reference; byRef only changes the label, not the tooltip.
findings.scenario: A reference-verified example with verification present but verified_by='reference' shows label 'gate.reference' yet tooltip 'gate.verified.tip' (fine); but a case with gates.verified=true and no verification object shows 'tipTodo' while the chip is green.
findings.fix: Base the tooltip on gates.verified_by and gates.verified rather than on the presence of verification.
